tells.1: Arranged lyricism: the em dash, “One of the lovely things,” and the mirrored Maybe lines.
tells.2: Stock specifics piled on to seem lived-in — Middlemarch, Mr. Okafor, a $38,000 GoFundMe, a retired-teacher bestseller — plus a so-thank-you glue sentence.
tells.3: “One of the lovely things … is that” is explanatory filler, and cutting the two-floors beat leaves the nostalgia floating.
tells.4: Rule-of-three “every shelf, every table, every book” and the paired “Maybe it’s been” sentences.

reason: Version 4 sounds most like a person editing their own posts: direct, even, and not performing loveliness or color. Version 2 has the liveliest lines, but the added names and figures feel inserted and the thank-you post is clumsy; 1 arranges the same beats into lyric copy, and 3 only flattens it.
